text: dsh-usage-heatmap 会在 DSH 网页侧栏添加使用热力图。它读取本机会话记录，按天展示近 30 天、90 天或一年的会话数和消息数。选择日期可以查看用户与助手消息、工具调用、Token 使用量、活跃时段、工作区及热门会话。格子深浅按消息数量区分，首次统计后会将每日计数缓存在 DSH_HOME 下，并在日志变化时更新。

dsh-usage-heatmap adds a heatmap panel to the DSH web sidebar. It shows daily session and message counts from local logs for 30, 90, or 365 days. Select a date to see messages, tools, tokens, hours, workspaces, and busy sessions. Counts are cached under DSH_HOME and refreshed when logs change.
想按天看看 DSH 最近的会话和消息使用量。
DSH 有没有能点开某一天查看工具调用和 Token 明细的日历？
I want a calendar view of my daily DSH session and message activity.
dsh-usage-heatmap 的功能「按日使用热力图」：在 DSH 网页侧栏打开近 30 天、90 天或一年的日历，按当天消息量显示格子深浅，并汇总会话与消息数量。选择日期后可加载当日活动明细。

dsh-usage-heatmap README · dsh-usage-heatmap：A [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-harness) Web UI plugin: one
left-sidebar entry that opens a full-panel **calendar heatmap** of daily session
and message counts, computed from the session logs this machine already stores.

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Features：- **A calendar, not a blank card.** Every day in the range is a visible square;
  a stretch with no usage still reads as a heatmap. Ranges: last 30 / 90 / 365
  days, laid out as Monday-to-Sunday week columns with month and weekday labels.
- **Grid first, data later.** The calendar is painted from local dates
  immediately (a skeleton of pale squares), and the counts only repaint the
  cells when they arrive. A failed load keeps the grid and shows the error
  inline with a retry button.
- **Each day opens up.** Selecting a cell expands a detail card below the
  calendar: the message split (user vs assistant), sessions (active vs newly
  created), tool calls plus the busiest tools, token usage (output and cache
  reads), the hour-by-hour activity shape with its peak, first/last activity and
  its span, the workspaces worked in, and the busiest sessions with their
  titles. The day's two headline numbers come from the calendar itself, so they
  paint instantly; the rest arrives from a dedicated per-day detail route.
- **Fast reopen.** Per-session day counts are cached on disk, so opening the
  panel only re-reads sessions whose log file changed — n

dsh-usage-heatmap README · What it counts：| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sessions` | logical sessions whose header `createdAt` falls on that day |
| `messages` | `user/message` + `assistant/message` events whose own `time` falls on that day, across every session on the machine |
| `detail` | for one selected day: user/assistant messages, active vs newly created sessions, tool calls, token usage, hourly activity, workspaces, busiest sessions |

dsh-usage-heatmap README · What it counts：Events before a forked/subagent session's `inheritedEventCount` are skipped, so
an inherited log prefix is not counted twice.

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Install：This package is a DSH **profile bundle** (`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`).
From a local checkout:

1. Quit DSH.
2. In the profile's `package.json` (for example
   `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`) add the dependency and list the
   bundle:

```json
   {
     "dependencies": {
       "dsh-usage-heatmap": "link:D:/dsh-usage-heatmap"
     },

A git checkout works the same way — point the dependency at the cloned
   directory.

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Install：3. Start DSH. The left sidebar gets the **使用热力图 / Usage heatmap** entry.

The checked-in `client.js` is already built, so a fresh checkout needs no
package install and no build to run. Only plugin development needs `pnpm`
(see [Development](#development)).

> If you previously installed an auto-generated local version of this plugin,
> disable or remove that entry first so the sidebar only shows one heatmap.

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Cache and the HTTP routes：The Host half reads sessions through `ctx.sessionQuery` and serves two JSON
routes:

```text
GET /_dsh/dsh-usage-heatmap/heatmap?from=<ms>&to=<ms>&tz=<minutes east>&refresh=1
GET /_dsh/dsh-usage-heatmap/detail?date=<YYYY-MM-DD>&tz=<minutes east>
```

Cache files live under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-usage-heatmap/`:

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Cache and the HTTP routes：- `cache-<account>.json` stores, per session, its message counts by day plus the
  log file identity (`mtime:size`) they came from.
- A request re-reads a session only when that identity changed; unchanged
  sessions are reused, a disappeared session drops out, and a failed re-read
  keeps the last good counts.
- Delete the cache files to force a full rebuild; `refresh=1` rebuilds once.

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Day detail route：Selecting a day asks the second route for that day's breakdown. It reuses the same rolling cache to decide which sessions were
active on that date, so a click re-reads only those logs — normally a handful —
instead of replaying the whole corpus. One response is bounded to the 150 most
active sessions of the day, plus the top tools, workspaces, sessions and models.
Titles and workspaces come from the session log itself (the latest
`session/title` event and the header `cwd`), and the client remembers each
day's answer for the rest of the page session. A day detail request after the
calendar has loaded does not rebuild the whole cache: it uses the same fresh
dataset the calendar request just wrote.

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Repository layout：```text
.
├── index.js                  # Host entry: re-exports the plugin from src/host/
├── client.js                 # Client entry, GENERATED from src/client/ by the build
├── src/

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Repository layout：The DSH Web client loads one lazy-CJS bundle per package (the `./client`
export), so `src/client/` is bundled ahead of time into the committed
`client.js`. The bundle only registers a factory with
`window.__ModuleLoader__`, exactly like a compiled DSH client plugin. The Host
half is plain Node ESM and runs straight from `src/host/`.

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Development：Requirements: Node.js (20+) and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install          # once: installs esbuild (dev-only)
pnpm run build        # bundle src/client/ -> client.js
pnpm test             # node:test suites (build first: they load client.js)
```

dsh-usage-heatmap README · Development：- **Client half:** edit `src/client/**`, run `pnpm run build`, restart DSH.
  `client.js` is generated — never edit it by hand.
- **Host half:** edit `src/host/**` and restart DSH; no build involved.
- `node scripts/build-client.mjs --sourcemap` keeps function names readable and
  emits `client.js.map` for debugging (not committed).

The Host half writes its cache on the first request, so the first open after a
cold cache rebuild may take a few seconds; later opens are incremental.
